document.title: Task 2 · University fees
document.text:
The cost of university can determine who is able to continue studying after school. I agree that financial circumstances should not prevent a capable student from obtaining a degree. However, I favour substantial support based on need rather than removing tuition fees for every student regardless of income.

The strongest reason for public funding is equal access. A young person from a low-income family may reject university because the prospect of debt is intimidating, even when a course would improve their opportunities. Scholarships that cover tuition and living costs can remove this barrier. Funding only the course itself may be insufficient: students still need somewhere to live and may have to reduce their paid working hours. Support should therefore reflect the actual cost of participation, not simply the price advertised by the institution.

Nevertheless, making every degree free would require resources that could otherwise support schools, healthcare or vocational training. Wealthier families would receive the same tuition subsidy as those unable to pay, even though their children already enjoy considerable advantages. A more targeted system could direct additional resources towards students facing the largest obstacles. This does not mean that other students should receive no assistance. Affordable loans with repayments linked to income can spread costs without demanding large payments before study begins.

Public investment should also depend on educational quality. Governments need to ensure that supported courses provide appropriate teaching and that students can make informed choices about their options. Simply increasing enrolment while allowing standards to fall would serve neither learners nor society. In conclusion, access to university deserves strong public support, but universal free tuition is not necessarily the fairest use of limited money. A combination of grants for those in need and manageable contributions from others would better reconcile opportunity with responsibility.
document.prompt:
WRITING TASK 2
Allow about 40 minutes.

University education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons and relevant examples. Write at least 250 words.
PPB! original practice material.

annotations.quote: The cost of university can determine who is able to continue studying after school.
annotations.label: Position
annotations.body: The answer supports access but rejects an unconditional subsidy. The contrast between need-based grants and universal free tuition is the central position.

annotations.quote: The strongest reason for public funding is equal access.
annotations.label: First argument
annotations.body: Living costs extend the access argument beyond tuition. The student who reduces paid work demonstrates why a fee-only policy may leave the barrier intact.

annotations.quote: Nevertheless, making every degree free would require resources that could otherwise support schools, healthcare or vocational training.
annotations.label: Development
annotations.body: The opportunity-cost argument compares tuition spending with schools and healthcare. Income-linked repayments provide an alternative rather than merely criticising free tuition.

annotations.quote: Public investment should also depend on educational quality.
annotations.label: Judgement
annotations.body: Quality safeguards connect funding to educational value. The final judgement maintains targeted support and manageable contributions.
